head: pr17394-r30
report:
No git. Read the eval portion of the diff (lines 450–1360), the subject of this commit.

Now the Python registry's acquireSession, waitForStartup, and starting path.

Writing a probe: gitignored unlistable dir at baseline, and node_modules / false-.git loss cases at delta time.

## DEFECT: Baseline capture now refuses a checkout that has an unlistable directory under a gitignored path (prior round's finding 2, baseline half, still open)

**Mechanism.** In `packages/coding-agent/src/task/worktree.ts`, `discoverNestedRepos` (lines 166–201) walks the whole working tree. It skips only `node_modules` and `.git`. Two checks in that walk now throw `IsolationCaptureIncompleteError`:
- any directory that `readdirTypedLookup` returns as `unknown` (lines 169–176);
- any `<dir>/.git` that `lstatLookup` returns as `unknown` (lines 189–191).

Both arrived with this patch. Before it, the walk wrapped `fs.readdir` in `catch { return; }`, and a `.git` it could not reach counted as "no repo". The walk does not consult `.gitignore`, but git never reads gitignored directories. So a directory git would never list now aborts the whole baseline.

**Where it bites.**
- `security/remediation.ts:31` calls `captureBaseline(repoRoot)` on the user's live checkout, so remediation refuses to start there.
- `captureIsolationBaseline` runs the same walk on the isolation dir. [INFERENCE: this matters for any backend that materialises ignored directories.]

**Trigger.** Put an ordinary gitignored cache owned by another uid, or at mode `0000`, in the checkout: `target/…`, `build/cache`, `.venv/…`, a Docker-written directory. Then call `captureBaseline` on that checkout.

**Measured.** Probe `scratch/…/capture.test.ts`, case D. The repo's `.gitignore` is `build/`, and `build/cache` is mode `0000`:
```
{"label":"D-ignored-build-cache","baseline":"raised: Could not read …/build/cache/.git: EACCES: permission denied, lstat '…"}
```
Git never looks inside `build/`, so the refusal protects nothing.

The delta half of the prior finding is closed. When the same directory appears after the baseline (case D2), the capture succeeds and carries `visible.txt`, because `captureDeltaPatch` no longer walks the tree:
```
{"label":"D2-ignored-appears-later","baseline":"ok","delta":"ok","hasVisible":true,"hasOnly":false}
```

**Fix.** Make the nested-repo walk skip what git ignores, for example with `git check-ignore`. Alternatively, find nested repos from git's own `ls-files --others --directory` output, which lists a nested repo as `sub/`, instead of erroring on any unlistable directory.

## NOT A DEFECT

**Prior findings, status at this head:**
- **Finding 1 (P1, five loss shapes) — CLOSED.** `assertTreeListable` is gone. `captureRepoDeltaPatch` now reads git's own stderr through `isolation-fs.ts:listUntracked` and refuses on any `could not open directory` line, or any other stderr line. I replayed four of the five shapes; every one now raises instead of returning a short patch:
  - C, untracked `node_modules/pkg/locked` at `0000`: `git could not read 1 director(y|ies) … node_modules/pkg/lo…`
  - L1 empty `.git` file, L3 plain `.git` directory, L4 dangling `.git` symlink: `… so this capture cannot say what is in them: sub/deep`
  - L2 (gitfile pointing nowhere) was not replayed. It goes through the same git-stderr path, so I expect the same result, but I did not observe it.
- **Finding 2 — delta half CLOSED, baseline half OPEN** (the defect above).
- **Finding 3 (P2, check-to-listing race) — CLOSED by construction.** The refusal now comes from the same `git ls-files` run that produces the listing, so there is no window between a check and the listing. I did not re-run the 400-trial race.
- **Finding 4 (P2, full-tree walk on every delta capture) — CLOSED.** `captureDeltaPatch` walks nothing. The baseline still walks once per run in `discoverNestedRepos`, as it did before this PR.
- **Finding 5 (P2, import-gate bypasses) — mostly CLOSED, not fully replayed.** `isolation-lookup-surface.test.ts` now:
  - parses the module graph with `Bun.Transpiler`, which closes the multiline-import case (J);
  - lists `"bun"` in `FS_MODULES`, closing G and L;
  - bans any `Bun` mention outside the surface instead of using a per-line allowlist, closing H;
  - scans the reachable graph instead of only the entry points, closing K.

  `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils` is allowed as a whole package, so a read helper exported from it would pass. I could not find a directory-read export in `packages/utils/src` within the time I had, so I do not assert this as a defect.
- **Finding 6 — CLOSED in the prior round.** Nothing in this head reopens it.

**This commit's subject (superseded-kernel reclaim), examined and cleared:**
- **Every `acquireSession` hold is released.** In both registries (`kernel-session-registry.ts`, `js/context-manager.ts`), every path that increments `activeUses` is matched by the decrement in `executeOnSession`'s / `executeInVmContext`'s `finally`. The Python descriptor defines no `waitForStartup`, so the session's creator can never be cancelled mid-startup and leave behind the `activeUses: 1` hold the session is born with. A startup that fails leaves `session` undefined and takes no hold.
- **Reaper re-arm logic is sound.** `SupersededKernelReaper`'s cancellation counter and generation number keep a deferred reclaim from re-arming after `cancel`/`cancelAll`. A borrow, or a running cell, defers the reclaim and is re-armed when it ends, through `reconcile*` in the release or `finally`.
- **Borrows target the same kernel the tools are found on.** `borrowEvalToolKernels` resolves identity with the same `resolvePythonKernelIdentity` / `resolveJsKernelIdentity` that `describeEvalTools` uses. The custom tools resolve identity again at call time; that was already the behaviour before this patch.
- **Workpool and subagent release paths are wired end to end.** The workpool's `onRelease` is a plain function. `runStructuredSubagent` wraps it in a `ReleaseHold`, and the lifecycle hand-over claims that hold through `asReleaseHold(...).claim()` in `agent-lifecycle.ts:267`, `executor.ts:3702` and `isolation-runner.ts:735`. Otherwise it is discharged in `runStructuredSubagent`'s `finally`. Nothing is dropped silently.
- **The new tests pass.** `bun test test/eval/kernel-session-registry.test.ts test/eval/js-superseded-context.test.ts`: 36 pass, 0 fail.

**Environment:** the probes ran as uid 1000 (not root), so the permission bits took effect.
